title: Career roadmap · HCI Researcher
summary: A research career focused on understanding human interaction with technology through experimental HCI, cognitive science, usability, behavioural research, interaction design and human-centred AI.

facts.Timeline assumption: 2026 is treated as Ph.D. Year 1. The roadmap assumes a research-heavy programme with experience in experimental design, qualitative and quantitative methods, interaction prototyping, statistical analysis and publication.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Develop from an individual researcher into a research leader who can define HCI agendas, supervise multidisciplinary teams and connect experimental evidence to product, societal and policy decisions. Maintain depth in research methods while adding AI evaluation, accessibility, multimodal interaction and responsible technology.

Career progression

Ph.D. Researcher → HCI Research Fellow → Postdoctoral/Research Scientist
2030–2035: HCI Research Scientist → Senior Researcher → Independent Research Lead
2035–2040: Senior/Principal HCI Researcher → Research Group Lead → HCI Research Director
2040–2046: Principal Scientist / Professor → HCI Research Centre Head → Research or Human-Centred AI Director
PhD routes
If further research is pursued after this Ph.D., relevant themes include:

The long-term objective is to become a recognised HCI research leader rather than simply an experienced UX researcher. That requires a distinctive research agenda, strong publications, reproducible research practices, successful collaborations and the ability to translate findings into better technologies. Emerging areas such as human–AI interaction, multimodal interfaces, accessibility, neuro-HCI and responsible AI can provide new research directions while preserving a strong HCI methodological core.
